title: Role of SPOP in cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure
projectDescription: Pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure involve profound remodeling of the myocardial proteome. To elucidate the role of the E3 adaptor protein SPOP in this process, we performed TMT-based quantitative proteomic analysis on left ventricular tissues collected four weeks after transverse aortic constriction (TAC) from Myh6-Cre control mice (n=5) and cardiac-specific SPOP knockout (cKO) mice (n=5).
sampleProcessingProtocol: Heart tissues were ground in liquid nitrogen and lysed in buffer (1% Triton X-100, 1% protease inhibitor cocktail), followed by sonication on ice. For PTM analysis, additional inhibitors (e.g., TSA, NAM, phosphatase inhibitors) were included. Lysates were centrifuged (12,000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C), and supernatants were precipitated with acetone (1:5, v/v), then washed and redissolved in 200 mM TEAB. Proteins were digested overnight with trypsin (1:50 w/w), reduced with 5 mM DTT, and alkylated with 11 mM iodoacetamide. Peptides were desalted using Strata X SPE columns. Peptides were separated using a home-made C18 analytical column (15 cm × 100 µm i.d.) on a Vanquish Neo UPLC system with a linear gradient of 4-99% acetonitrile (0.1% formic acid) at 600 nL/min.
dataProcessingProtocol: MS analysis was performed on a timsTOF HT mass spectrometer (Bruker) in DIA-PASEF mode. MS1 scan range was m/z 300-1500, with 12 PASEF MS/MS scans per cycle. MS2 scan range was m/z 395-1080, with a 15 m/z isolation window. DIA data were processed using DIA-NN (v1.8) against the Mus musculus UniProt database (UP_20241025, 84,204 entries) with a reverse decoy. Trypsin/P was set as the digestion enzyme, allowing up to 1 missed cleavage. Carbamidomethylation (Cys) and N-terminal Met excision were set as fixed modifications. A false discovery rate (FDR) of < 5% was applied. padj < 0.05 and |foldchange| > 1.5 were set as the threshold for significantly differential expression.
